priceSnapshot.note: Up 540.3 points and 0.70 percent on 24 hours against the 77,120.1 close of the 13 September 06:00Z bar, and up 988.6 points and 1.29 percent against the 76,671.8 endday mark. The whole gain was made in a single three-hour window: 76,805.0 at the 00:00Z close to 77,598.3 at the 02:00Z close, then a grind to the 77,893.8 high on the 06:00Z bar. Price has since given back 233.4 points of that high.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 77,199.7, the 1Dutc EMA20, 460.7 points under the mark. This is the same level the endday report made its add trigger and it is the whole thesis of this report: eight consecutive settled hourly closes have now held above it. Losing it again on a settled close - not a wick - means the overnight reclaim was another liquidity event and the 12 to 14 September chop band reasserts. Trim the tranche added tonight on that close. The 1H EMA20 at 77,322.7 and EMA50 at 77,287.7 sit between here and there and should break first; treat them as the warning, the daily average as the trigger.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 77,958.5, the 1H EMA200, 298.1 points above the mark. That single level clears the entire ceiling in one move: the 4H EMA50 at 77,855.42, the 77,893.8 session high, and the 77,700 to 77,900 short-liquidation stack all sit beneath it. Nothing above 77,700 has been tested twice, so a settled close through 77,958.5 is the first evidence since 11 September that the 4H frame has flipped rather than merely bounced. Anything less than a settled hourly close there is a wick into spent fuel - the 06:00Z bar already traded to 77,893.8 and closed 303.1 points lower.

decisionBox.changed: Bias flips from the endday's range-with-a-BEARISH-tilt back to range-with-a-BULLISH-tilt, and position from REDUCE to ADD. The endday report set an add trigger at a settled 1H close above 77,023.5, the 1Dutc EMA20; the 01:00Z bar closed 77,107.7, 84.2 points through it, and seven further bars have confirmed. Its reduce gate at 76,394.9 never fired - the lowest settled close after the mark was 76,805.0, short by 410.1 points, and the post-mark low of 76,642.5 never even reached the level on the wick. Its recommended 76,280.0 stop was not filled. So the endday got the gates right and the discretionary call wrong: it trimmed 12 percent of spot at 76,671.8 and price is 988.6 points higher. Confidence is 5.75 rather than higher for two reasons that have nothing to do with the chart. Brent has gapped from 104.61 to 107.57, plus 2.83 percent, on Gulf and Red Sea supply disruption, and the FOMC decides on 16 September with roughly 85 percent priced for a 25bp hike. An inflationary energy shock two days before a hawkish meeting is not a backdrop that pays for leverage, and the long/short account ratio at 1.55 says the crowd is already leaning the way this report leans.

liquidityMagnet.note: Measured realized liquidations - fuel already spent, not a forward resting-order heatmap. The polarity has flipped completely from the endday read. That report measured 958,020 USD of LONG liquidations, 99.1 percent one-sided, stacked BELOW spot. This window measures 419,400 USD of SHORT liquidations against 18,726 USD of longs, 95.7 percent one-sided the other way, stacked in three consecutive bands from 77,700 to 77,900 ABOVE the mark. That is what the overnight run was: shorts being force-bought, not buyers arriving. The nearestBelow of 77,600 is a technicality - 2 fills and 1,653 USD - and the first band under spot with any size is 77,400 at 13,053 USD, which is 3.1 percent of the upside total. The pull reads up because the measured flow is up, but the honest caveat is that spent short fuel does not squeeze twice: open interest is 2.175 billion USD against 2.139 billion at the endday mark, UP 1.70 percent, so the book was rebuilt rather than burned down, and it was rebuilt long - the account ratio sits at 1.55.

calibration.rollingRecord: Gates over the last six publications: 1 reduce fired of 6, 2 adds fired of 6. Tonight is the second add to fire in that span and it fired cleanly - 84.2 points through on the first settled close and seven confirming bars behind it, with no wick-versus-close ambiguity of the kind that muddied both of midday's gates. Discretionary calls stand at 4 green of the last 6; the endday REDUCE joins midday's ADD as the second consecutive discretionary miss, and the two missed in opposite directions within six hours of each other.
calibration.note: The endday's 76,394.9 reduce gate did NOT fire and was not close. It required a settled 1H close below the level; the lowest settled close after the 00:42Z mark was 76,805.0 on the 00:00Z bar, 410.1 points short, and the post-mark low of 76,642.5 never touched the gate on the wick either - it held 247.6 points above. The 76,001.0 invalidation was 641.6 points away at its nearest. The recommended resting stop at 76,280.0 was NOT filled, clearing the low by 362.5 points, and that call was correct for the second session running. The 77,023.5 add gate DID fire: the 01:00Z bar closed 77,107.7, 84.2 points through, followed by 77,598.3, 77,593.4, 77,674.1, 77,608.9, 77,590.7 and the live 77,660.4 - eight closes, none of them retracing below the trigger. Discretionary: the endday TRIMMED 12 percent of the spot book at 76,671.8 to raise cash into the gap. Spot marks 77,660.4, so that trim gave up 988.6 points and 1.29 percent on roughly 19.6 USDT of stock, about minus 0.25 USDT of opportunity, and the core it was de-risking is now worth more than when it was cut. Hence false. What the endday got wrong is worth naming precisely, because it is the same error midday made in reverse. It read 958,020 USD of one-sided LONG liquidations with open interest DOWN 1.48 percent and concluded the magnet below would be eaten. Both halves of that were true and the conclusion still failed, because a 99-percent one-sided flush with falling open interest is a book that has just been emptied - which is the setup for a reversal, not a continuation. The report actually wrote that sentence about the squeeze risk and declined to short for exactly that reason, then trimmed spot anyway, which is the same trade in smaller size. The lesson is not to read the map better; it is that when the liquidation tape is 99 percent one-sided and open interest is falling, the move is finished rather than starting.
